newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cert stocks fall to new all-time lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cert stocks fall to new all-time lows.

text.p: U.S. certified coffee stocks, already at their lowest level at least 16 years, declined once again last week, falling by 150 60-kg bags to a mere 321 bags, the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange said Monday.

The latest drawdown brings exchange-certified inventories to the lowest level since the CSCE began tracking stocks in 1980. The CSCE also reported there were 1,250 bags pending grading in Miami, the same number as last week.
While the stock numbers served as yet another confirmation that near-terms supplies remain tight, traders were generally unfazed by the latest decline.
"Half of nothing is nothing," said one New York-based trader.
The weekly CSCE drawdown comes on the heels of monthly consumer inventory data released last Friday, showing a sharp drawdown in U.S. warehouse coffee stocks.
U.S. supplies of green coffee fell by 351,000 60-kg bags in October, to 1,260,000 bags, the lowest level since the Green Coffee Association of New York began tracking inventories in January, 1988.

Open interest in the spot December contract, which goes into month-long notice period Tuesday, was still relatively high as of Friday at 3,675 lots, the equivalent of more than 900,000 bags of coffee.
